items.title: Show HN: Can you tell a real tweet of a certain user from an AI one?
items.contentSnippet:
Just a small game I coded up for research.
After some limited tests, people tend to pick the AI-written post as the
real one more than 55% of the time, almost 60%.
So apparently LLMs kinda pass the Turing test when it comes to social media
posts and not even general social media posts, but posts of a specific user!?

items.title: Show HN: Snag, a small HTTP regression test runner
items.contentSnippet:
For a personal project, I needed a small and lightweight HTTP regression test runner. Hurl was the closest thing I found, but I needed real scripting in my assertions. So I wrote Snag, It's written in Rust and uses TOML for test definitions and Rhai for assertions and scripting. It's pretty early in development but it's usable. If you have any feedback, criticism or suggestions please let me know.

items.title: Digital Fluency Is the Missing Foundation in K-12 Career Pathways
items.contentSnippet:
What separates a student who can use a digital tool from one who can build something new with it? Kimberly Smith of Digital Promise argues that digital fluency, not just digital literacy, is the foundational skill K-12 career pathways have been missing. Drawing on credentialed cybersecurity programs in rural Alabama and a six-part fluency framework, this piece offers a clear, actionable case for why every career pathway, in every industry, must embed digital fluency now.
The post Digital Fluency
